correctness.rationale: Radial normalization is exact: Gamma(d,1) and chi-square(d) match second moments. The log radial density ratio is a strictly concave quadratic. Equal mass and equal quadratic moment rule out an origin ratio >=1; equal mass forces a strictly positive interior maximum, hence exactly two density intersections. Integrating the +,-,+ density difference yields exactly one nontrivial CDF zero and strict side order. At r=d+c the uniform central Gamma expansion provides the linear sign limit, giving uniquely c=(4+3sqrt(2))/6. Numerical checker tests 10,963 finite assertions only and is not used as an infinite proof. No boundary or application extension is claimed.

value.rationale: Comparing dispersal kernels with matched mean-squared displacement is natural for unbiased spatial spread. The theorem identifies the exact source-centered target radius at which short-range landing advantage becomes long-range landing advantage in every higher dimension, with a sharp additive large-d location, rather than merely comparing kernel shapes or finitely sampled radii. This resolves a structural probability ordering question relevant as a theoretical dispersal benchmark; it does not claim biological validity in arbitrarily high dimensions.
